blocks.x: Prior authorization turnaround down 62% — clinical evidence assembled automatically

A national health insurer — a Healthcare & Life Sciences engagement delivered by a blended Dataq Software team under the outcome-linked engagement model. Identity withheld as standard; the figures are the client's, reproduced with permission.
Prior-auth requests bounced for evidence that existed in clinical notes; SLA breaches and provider revolt.
Claims codes and clinical narratives never reconciled; coding integrity audits painful. Medical-policy grounding inconsistent across decision paths.

The prior-auth agent maps policy criteria to chart evidence, assembles submissions and appeals with citations, and routes true judgment calls to clinicians. Claims-clinical reconciliation on Forge now feeds coding-integrity and quality reporting with lineage; coverage decisions cite policy passages with provenance on Nexus.

items: human checkpoints sat exactly where the risk register wanted them — designed, not improvised.
lineage and freshness were design constraints from week one, so the measurement never became the controversy.
answers were grounded and cited from the first release, which is what made the rest of the program defensible.

blocks.x: If the national health insurer program reads like your own estate, the honest advice is: start with the baseline diagnostic, not with the build.
